customer_patience.description: Starting patience of each new customer, 0.2 (already on edge) to 1 (relaxed). Lower values reach anger sooner and make the ticket harder.
customer_patience.adjustment_guide: relax 0.85-1.0, focus 0.6-0.75, grit 0.3-0.45, empathy 0.4-0.55. Applies to the next ticket. Move by at most 0.15 at a time.

hostility.description: How fast patience drains on a setback (a denial, a repeated question, a slow reply) and how sharp the customer's wording gets. Higher is harder.
hostility.adjustment_guide: relax 0-0.15, focus 0.25-0.4, grit 0.6-0.8, empathy 0.5-0.7. Applies to the next ticket. Move by at most 0.2 at a time.

ambiguity.description: How much of what the customer knows they withhold until asked. At 0 the opener states the problem fully; at 1 the agent has to draw every detail out. Higher is harder and rewards good questions.
ambiguity.adjustment_guide: relax 0-0.2, focus 0.3-0.5, grit 0.6-0.9, curiosity 0.5-0.8. Applies to the next ticket.

concurrency.description: How many tickets are open at once. Above 1 the agent switches between conversations with separate customers, names and order numbers. Higher is harder and loads working memory and attention.
concurrency.adjustment_guide: relax 1, focus 2, grit 3, collaborate 2. Applies at once: a raise pulls the next ticket from the queue immediately. Change by one step at a time.

policy_complexity.description: Which version of the policy document applies: 1 is short with no exceptions, 3 is long with exceptions and limits the agent must check. Higher is harder.
policy_complexity.adjustment_guide: relax 1, focus 1-2, grit 3. Applies to the next ticket.

incongruence_rate.description: Probability that a ticket's customer sounds angrier than their words read: the text stays neutral and only the voice carries the mood. Only matters with voice on. Higher tests emotional attunement.
incongruence_rate.adjustment_guide: empathy 0.5-1.0, otherwise 0-0.2. Applies to the next ticket.

speech_rate.description: Speaking rate of the customer voice. Higher is faster and harder to follow.
speech_rate.adjustment_guide: relax 0.9, focus 1.0, grit 1.15-1.3. Applies to the next spoken line.

interruption_rate.description: Probability that the customer talks over the agent's reply in voice mode. Higher tests turn-taking under pressure. No effect in text mode.
interruption_rate.adjustment_guide: relax 0, focus 0-0.2, grit 0.4-0.7. Applies to the next ticket.

policy_switch.description: When 1, the next ticket carries a mid-conversation policy update (a banner and a changed rule) the agent must notice and apply. Tests cognitive flexibility.
policy_switch.adjustment_guide: grit 1, curiosity 1, otherwise 0. Applies to the next ticket.

adjustment_instructions:
You are adjusting parameters for Support Desk, a customer-support simulation. The player is the agent on a help desk; simulated customers arrive in a queue with a problem, a mood (calm, tense, angry, resigned, shown as a badge and a patience bar) and sometimes a false belief about what they are owed. The player reads the policy panel, talks to the customer in a chat transcript, uses account tools (some of which are against policy for the case at hand), and closes each ticket with a declared confidence that it was resolved.

Each frame shows the queue and policy on the left, the conversation and composer in the middle, the tools and customer card on the right, and the score, tickets done and shift clock in the header. The transcript text is in the events: AGENT_MESSAGE (text, latencyMs, turn), CUSTOMER_REPLY (text, affect, patience), TOOL_CALL (tool, args, ok), AFFECT_CHANGE (from, to, trigger), POLICY_VIOLATION (rule, severity), POLICY_SWITCH, BELIEF_CORRECTED, TICKET_SWITCH, CONFUSION, HOLD, TICKET_CLOSED (resolution, declaredConfidence, rTau, csat, violations) and SHIFT_SUMMARY.

Nine parameters are exposed: customer_patience (0.2-1, starting patience, lower is harder), hostility (0-1, how fast patience drains and how sharp the wording gets), ambiguity (0-1, how much the customer withholds until asked), concurrency (1-3 tickets open at once, applies immediately), policy_complexity (1-3, length and exceptions in the policy), incongruence_rate (0-1, voice angrier than the words, voice mode only), speech_rate (0.8-1.3, voice mode), interruption_rate (0-1, voice mode) and policy_switch (0/1, a mid-ticket rule change on the next ticket). All but concurrency and speech_rate apply to the NEXT ticket.

Given the player's current flow state, skill metrics, and target mood, output parameter values that guide the player toward the target mood:
- For 'relax': customer_patience ~0.95, hostility ~0.05, ambiguity ~0.1, concurrency 1, policy_complexity 1, policy_switch 0: calm customers who say what they need.
- For 'focus': customer_patience ~0.7, hostility ~0.3, ambiguity ~0.4, concurrency 2, policy_complexity 1-2, policy_switch 0: two conversations that reward attention and good questions.
- For 'grit': customer_patience ~0.35, hostility ~0.7, ambiguity ~0.6, concurrency 3, policy_complexity 3, policy_switch 1: hostile, pushy customers, a dense policy and a rule that changes under the player.
- For 'empathy': customer_patience ~0.45, hostility ~0.6, ambiguity ~0.3, concurrency 1, incongruence_rate ~0.7: one upset customer at a time, where the mood matters more than the speed.
- For 'collaborate': concurrency 2, customer_patience ~0.7, hostility ~0.3.
- For 'curiosity': ambiguity ~0.7, policy_switch 1, concurrency 1.

Consider the player's current performance: repeated POLICY_VIOLATION events mean the policy is too dense or the pressure too high; lower policy_complexity first, then hostility. AFFECT_CHANGE events that only go toward angry, with no recovery, mean the player is not acknowledging the customer; lower hostility and raise customer_patience so there is room to practise. CONFUSION events mean concurrency is too high; drop it by one. Long AGENT_MESSAGE latencies with short replies suggest overload; drop concurrency or ambiguity. If every ticket closes resolved with high declared confidence and CSAT at or above 4, raise challenge: concurrency by one, then ambiguity, then policy_switch.

Always adjust gradually from the current values: at most 0.15 on customer_patience, 0.2 on hostility, 0.2 on ambiguity, one step on concurrency and policy_complexity, and flip policy_switch at most once per two tickets.
skill_adjustment_instructions:
Support Desk exercises verbal reasoning (explaining a policy in the customer's terms), planning (the order of lookups and actions to a resolution), task switching and attention (several open tickets with different names and order numbers), memory (holding what the customer already said without asking again), deduction (telecom troubleshooting from symptoms to cause), knowledge (applying the policy document, including after it changes), timing (reply latency the customer feels) and action (correct tool use). Read the transcript from the AGENT_MESSAGE and CUSTOMER_REPLY events, not from the frames.

Per-skill levers (primary first):
- verbal: raise ambiguity and hostility so explanations have to be clear and acknowledging; keep concurrency at 1.
- planning and deduction: raise policy_complexity and ambiguity; prefer telecom tickets; keep hostility moderate so the reasoning, not the mood, is the challenge.
- task-switching and attention: raise concurrency one step at a time; watch CONFUSION and TICKET_SWITCH events.
- memory: raise ambiguity (more facts to gather and hold) and concurrency.
- knowledge: set policy_switch 1 and policy_complexity 2-3.
- timing: raise concurrency and hostility together so slow replies cost patience.

Move one or two parameters per adjustment, by the same small steps as the mood guidance.
event_skill_guidance: Score from the events, which carry the full transcript; the frames show the layout only. AGENT_MESSAGE text that cites the policy correctly, in the customer's terms, is knowledge and verbal; text that states the new rule after a POLICY_SWITCH is knowledge and task-switching, text that states the old rule after it is a knowledge failure. TOOL_CALL with ok=true and arguments that match what the customer gave is planning and action; a TOOL_CALL that triggers POLICY_VIOLATION is an action failure regardless of the customer's pressure. Correct tool order (lookup before action) is planning. AGENT_MESSAGE with a short latencyMs and a correct reply is perceptual-speed and timing; long latencies with concurrency above 1 are an attention load, not a failure, unless CONFUSION fires. Recalling details the customer gave earlier without re-asking is memory; a CUSTOMER_REPLY of 'I already told you that' is a memory failure. Diagnosing a telecom fault with few TOOL_CALLs before the fix is deduction. AFFECT_CHANGE toward calm after an acknowledging AGENT_MESSAGE is verbal. BELIEF_CORRECTED is deduction and verbal. TICKET_SWITCH followed by a correct reply with no CONFUSION is task-switching. Chunks with no AGENT_MESSAGE and no TOOL_CALL are the player reading; do not score skills from them.
notes: Parameters mirror static/src/params.js; keep the two in step. Keys 1-9 in GameAdjustmentTester and static/iframeTest.html send the presets listed there. event_skill_guidance is what makes the screenshot scorer read the conversation; the frames are a chat UI and carry little on their own.
